issues.description: coerceNumber silently maps null/NaN domain entries to 0 instead of propagating NaN as before.
issues.detail: Original code used toNumber, which returned null and produced NaN through arithmetic. The new coerceNumber's `?? 0` swaps in a default, changing observable output for malformed inputs. This is a behavior change buried in a 'just added types' PR. Either preserve NaN propagation or call out the semantic shift explicitly in the commit message.

issues.description: Domain typed as number[] but invariant is actually NonEmptyArray (and effectively length >= 2).
issues.detail: The functions require domain[0] and the last element as distinct endpoints, but the public signature accepts number[]. A stricter type would push the check to compile time and make the runtime throw a real backstop. The current half-typed signature understates the invariant the implementation depends on.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the isNonEmpty guard fires inside pan/zoom.
issues.detail: panLog and zoomLog call Math.sign(domain[0]) before delegating, so an empty domain yields sign=NaN before the inner throw triggers. Tests only cover Linear. Pull the non-empty check to the public boundary so the invariant holds once, and add tests for Log/Pow/Symlog empty-domain paths.

issues.description: Local identity shadows the existing accessors.identity import without justification.
issues.detail: The old file imported identity from accessors.js. The new file defines a typed local identity and drops the import, duplicating a shared utility under a narrower numeric type. Either reuse the shared identity or add a one-line comment explaining the narrower-typed local.

issues.description: Empty-domain throw is a new policy decision smuggled into a typing-only refactor.
issues.detail: The PR claims same runtime behavior but introduces a thrown error for empty domains, where callers previously got NaN propagation. That is a separate precondition change deserving its own commit and a note for downstream callers. Separate the policy change from the typing pass.

issues.description: peek overload only narrows for callers with tuple types; intent should be documented.
issues.detail: The non-empty overload `peek<T>(array: readonly [T, ...T[]]): T` fires only when callers have already proven non-emptiness in the type system. Internal pan/zoom callers pass number[], so peek still returns number|undefined and undefined silently coerces to NaN. Add a comment explaining the overload's intended use or drop it.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR is mostly a clean TS port but quietly changes value semantics: coerceNumber's `?? 0` replaces toNumber's null-returning behavior, and a new empty-domain throw is policy disguised as typing. All three reviewers flag the silent NaN-to-0 shift as the headline concern. The Domain type is also too loose — number[] understates the real NonEmptyArray (effectively length >= 2) invariant the implementation depends on. The non-empty check should be pulled to the public boundary so panLog/zoomLog don't read domain[0] before the guard fires, and tests should cover Log/Pow/Symlog paths, not just Linear.
